title: [Bug]: CANN feature detection can use different ACL headers from extension build
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM Ascend source: current `main` after #16256
- CANN: 9.2.0 (`V100R001C12SPC001B200`)
- Python: 3.11.10
- PyTorch: 2.10.0
- torch_npu: 2.10.0.post4
- SOC: `ascend950pr_9599`

### Describe the bug

The CMake feature probe for `aclrtGetPhyDevIdByUserDevId` uses only `${ASCEND_HOME_PATH}/include`, but the `vllm_ascend_C` extension currently searches `${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include` before that directory.

Some torch_npu wheels contain an older snapshot of the ACL headers. If that snapshot exposes `acl/acl_rt.h`, CMake detects the API in the selected CANN toolkit and defines `CANN_DEVICE_ID_MAPPING`, while the actual extension build loads the older torch_npu copy and fails:

```text
csrc/torch_binding.cpp:94:16: error: 'aclrtGetPhyDevIdByUserDevId' was not declared in this scope; did you mean 'aclrtGetPhyDevIdByLogicDevId'?
```

Both header copies use the same include guard, so the newer CANN header cannot add the missing declaration after the stale copy has been included.

The outcome currently depends on wheel layout. A torch_npu wheel that keeps its ACL snapshot below `include/third_party/acl/inc` may build successfully because `-I${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include` does not directly resolve `acl/acl_rt.h`. A wheel that exposes the snapshot from its include search path fails from a clean build.

The following official PyPI aarch64 CPython 3.11 wheels were inspected directly. None of their bundled ACL headers declares `aclrtGetPhyDevIdByUserDevId`; the affected versions are the ones that expose the stale header at `torch_npu/include/acl/acl_rt.h`.

| torch_npu package | Bundled `acl_rt.h` location | Result before this fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `2.10.0`, `2.10.0.post2`, `2.10.0.post4` | `include/third_party/acl/inc/acl/acl_rt.h` | No direct collision with `-I${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include` |
| `2.10.0.post6` | `include/acl/acl_rt.h` | Affected |
| `2.9.0.post6`, `2.7.1.post8` | `include/third_party/acl/inc/acl/acl_rt.h` | No direct collision with `-I${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include` |
| `2.9.0.post8`, `2.7.1.post10` | `include/acl/acl_rt.h` | Affected |
| `2.11.0`, `2.12.0` | `include/third_party/acl/inc/acl/acl_rt.h` | No direct collision with `-I${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include` |

Custom or internally repackaged wheels can differ, so the installed header path is the definitive check. The official compatibility matrix maps `2.10.0.post6` to CANN 9.1.X; using it with CANN 9.2 is outside that published pairing, but the extension should still use the same selected CANN headers as its feature probes.

### Reproduction

1. Use a CANN toolkit whose `acl/acl_rt.h` declares `aclrtGetPhyDevIdByUserDevId`.
2. Put a stale ACL snapshot without that declaration under a directory passed as `${TORCH_NPU_PATH}/include`.
3. Configure the project. The feature probe succeeds.
4. Build `csrc/torch_binding.cpp`. Compilation fails with the error above.

### Expected behavior

The native extension should compile against the same selected CANN headers used by the feature checks. `${ASCEND_HOME_PATH}/include` should take precedence over the ACL snapshot bundled with torch_npu.

This was found while validating the device mapping code merged in #16256 and a subsequent clean build of #16249.

body:
### Your current environment

Sanitized excerpt only: **I did not run `collect_env.py` for this submission**. The following comes from preserved environment/source evidence, not fabricated collect-env output.

- Ascend A3; DSV4 Flash W8A8, hybrid memory attention (HMA); 16 logical NPUs per P/D role, P DP4/TP4 and D DP16/TP1; dspark with 5 speculative tokens; maximum model length 524288.
- Public image tag: `quay.nju.edu.cn/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.26.0rc1-a3`.
- Inspected vLLM-Ascend revision: `f2f74a16c3c50a76f4349d807918e83edec1e35c`; vLLM revision: `568afb3a13806beb53bb2e6bd518269357b237c0`.
- Mooncake NPU package `0.3.11.post1`; corresponding inspected source revision `e9c61075720039bcfc5fffd19f847608402be3d0`.
- The original incident binary hash was not preserved. Evidence was collected from a rebuilt environment using the same image tag: current actual source/stack line numbers match the incident; Mooncake C++ log line numbers match the pinned source. This is source/version alignment, **not byte-for-byte provenance of the original binary**, and not a claim of reproduction on clean current main.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Scope: the Hybrid connector can report receive completion after a negative transfer result without reporting the failed destination blocks.** This is a reproducible connector failure-contract defect; it is not a claim that the original device error 507035 has been reproduced or causally explained.

At the pinned revision, [`mooncake_hybrid_connector.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/f2f74a16c3c50a76f4349d807918e83edec1e35c/vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_hybrid_connector.py#L591):

1. `_transfer_kv_cache_all_groups` calls `batch_transfer_sync_read`; `ret < 0` raises `RuntimeError` (lines 699–706).
2. `_handle_request` catches the exception and only logs it (599–607).
3. Its `finally` still marks the task done; when the request's task-count/final-marker conditions are met, it updates the completion tracker. It also sends `DONE_RECVING` to the producer (608–619). Producer page release remains conditional on its existing reader-count protocol; this is not a claim that every failure instantly releases every page.
4. This connector file does not override `get_block_ids_with_load_errors`, so the inherited default returns an empty set.

The [vLLM base contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/568afb3a13806beb53bb2e6bd518269357b237c0/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py#L375) requires asynchronous failed requests still to appear in `get_finished()`, with their failed blocks reported **no later than that same forward pass**. A same-round finished/invalid snapshot is one implementation strategy. The defect is missing failed-block information, **not `finished` by itself**. MultiConnector aggregation cannot reconstruct information that was never reported. Once global completion and other scheduler conditions hold, the request can be treated as a successful KV load; the historical incident does not prove all those conditions across every rank.

#### Self-contained CPU reproduction against actual pinned functions

Run with Python 3.10+ and public-network access. It downloads the pinned public source, AST-extracts the actual transfer/handler/tracker functions, and mocks only external dependencies. Synthetic addresses are never dereferenced; no model, NPU, or service is started. This is a deterministic function-level reproduction, not end-to-end model inference. The harness is included below.

```python
import ast, urllib.request, logging, threading, queue, time
from collections import defaultdict, OrderedDict
from types import SimpleNamespace
COMMIT = 'f2f74a16c3c50a76f4349d807918e83edec1e35c'
PATH = 'vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_p2p/mooncake_hybrid_connector.py'
# Execute original AST functions; source is Apache-2.0, copyright contributors
# to the vllm-ascend project. No source implementation is copied into this harness.
url = f'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/{COMMIT}/{PATH}'
source = urllib.request.urlopen(url).read().decode()
tree = ast.parse(source)
ns = dict(OrderedDict=OrderedDict, threading=threading, time=time, logger=logging.getLogger('repro'),
          envs=SimpleNamespace(VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=60),
          MambaSpec=type('MambaSpec', (), {}),
          group_concurrent_contiguous=lambda r,l: ([r],[l]))
def extract(name, methods):
    cls = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n,ast.ClassDef) and n.name==name)
    body = [n for n in cls.body if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in methods]
    assert len(body)==len(methods)
    mod = ast.Module(body=[ast.ImportFrom(module='__future__', names=[ast.alias(name='annotations')], level=0),
        ast.ClassDef(name=name,bases=[],keywords=[],body=body,decorator_list=[])],type_ignores=[])
    exec(compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(mod),url,'exec'),ns)
    return ns[name]
Tracker = extract('KVCacheTaskTracker',['__init__','add_req_to_process','update_done_task_count','get_and_clear_finished_requests','_retrieve_expired_requests'])
Recv = extract('KVCacheRecvingThread',['_handle_request','_mark_request_task_submitted','_mark_request_task_done','_transfer_kv_cache_all_groups'])
r=Recv(); r.use_hybrid=True
r.request_task_counts=defaultdict(int);r.finished_request_markers=set()
r.request_task_counts_lock=threading.Lock();r.task_tracker=Tracker();r.task_tracker.add_req_to_process('r')
r.proc_not_transfer_request_lock=threading.Lock();r.proc_not_transfer_request={'p':True}
r.request_queue=queue.Queue();r.request_queue.put('r');signals=[]
r._send_done_signal_to_free_remote_port=lambda *a:signals.append('free-port')
r._send_done_recv_signal=lambda *a:signals.append('DONE_RECVING')
r.remote_metadata_lock=threading.Lock()
r.kv_caches_base_addr={'remote':{1:[1000]},'local':{2:[2000]}}
r.remote_te_port={'remote':{1:3}};r.local_engine_id='local';r.local_handshake_port=2
r.hma_group_size=1;r.kv_cache_specs=[object()];r.addr_group_idx=[]
r.block_len_per_addr=[16];r.block_stride_per_addr=[16];r.tp_rank=0
calls=[]
def fail(*args): calls.append(args);return -1
r.engine=SimpleNamespace(batch_transfer_sync_read=fail)
m=dict(request_id='r',remote_request_id='p',remote_host='127.0.0.1',remote_handshake_port=1,
       remote_port_send_num={},all_task_done=True,local_block_ids=[[1]],remote_block_ids=[[2]],remote_engine_id='remote')
r._mark_request_task_submitted(m);r._handle_request(m)
finished=r.task_tracker.get_and_clear_finished_requests()
overrides=[n.name for c in tree.body if isinstance(c,ast.ClassDef) for n in c.body
           if isinstance(n,ast.FunctionDef) and n.name=='get_block_ids_with_load_errors']
print('transfer_calls=',len(calls),'finished=',sorted(finished),'signals=',signals,'load_error_overrides=',overrides)
assert len(calls)==1 and finished=={'r'} and signals==['free-port','DONE_RECVING'] and not overrides
```

Observed locally for this submission (exit 0 verifies that the problematic original behavior is present):

```text
RuntimeError: Mooncake transfer failed, ret: -1
transfer_calls= 1 finished= ['r'] signals= ['free-port', 'DONE_RECVING'] load_error_overrides= []
```

The caught traceback is `_handle_request` line 604 -> `_transfer_kv_cache_all_groups` line 706 -> the RuntimeError above. The source filename is the pinned public URL used by `compile`; no deployment paths are needed. DEBUG/TRACE model logging was not newly enabled for this report.

#### Candidate experiment and the separate HMA limitation

Preserved CPU tests execute actual AST-extracted source: the original source fails the candidate safety assertions (exit 1), while the local candidate passes 18 deterministic cases (exit 0); original evidence hashes remained unchanged. Cases include negative results/exceptions, earlier-task failure followed by later success, atomic finished/invalid bookkeeping, real DONE/ACK helper behavior, cancellation retention, and multi-reader producer completion.

A separate [scheduler limitation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/568afb3a13806beb53bb2e6bd518269357b237c0/vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py#L2693) matters to a fix: `_update_requests_with_invalid_blocks` uses single-group unpacking with a TODO for HMA. An actual-function test with two KV groups raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 1)`. The fail-policy path still invokes this helper. This is a compatibility constraint on recovery, not the cause of the negative transfer or a complete explanation of the original crash.

Our **local experimental candidate, not an upstream fix**, uses a matching experimental Mooncake ABI to distinguish a drained logical failure (`-2`) from unknown quiescence (`-1`). It keeps internal finished/invalid bookkeeping, but deliberately raises from worker `get_finished` on failure instead of publishing a normal failed HMA result into that incompatible scheduler. Unknown failures latch local fatal state and withhold subsequent local submissions and DONE/finished publication.

This is **not production-ready**: there is no global rank fence, worker exceptions/process exit do not prove device or remote quiescence, concurrent batches need separate lifetime accounting, DONE lacks epoch/deduplication guarantees, and the candidate serializes receiving work. Full engine failure propagation, cross-rank containment, memory retirement, and performance remain unverified. The 18 CPU tests are not a faulted-model or original-507035 reproduction.

#### Related transport lifecycle report

[Mooncake#4247](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/issues/4247) reports the separate synchronous outer-timeout/quiescence contract, including controlled real-NPU delayed-submit results. A connector fix must account for that lifetime boundary, but neither report proves the historical 507035 root cause.

#### Expected behavior / maintainer questions

- Preserve destination load failures through task aggregation and honor the finished/invalid-block contract.
- Separate logical request failure from proof that a transport has stopped touching source/destination memory. A negative synchronous return alone is insufficient to release ownership if the transport can remain active.
- For unsupported HMA recovery, fail explicitly with coordinated containment rather than silently treating bad KV as successfully received. A local exception alone does not implement that coordination.

Related reports: [#5660](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/5660), [#13439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/13439), and [#9220](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/9220) describe related transfer/output symptoms, not proof of an identical root cause. [#15420](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/15420) concerns producer TTL expiry before a later pull, a different trigger. I reviewed [vllm#55870](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55870): it concerns generic Mooncake P2P bootstrap/remote-wait error propagation; this report isolates the Ascend Hybrid negative-return/completion contract with pinned actual-function evidence. These should not be merged into one asserted root cause.

title: [Guide] MegaMoe validation environment on CANN 9.2.0: package set and install steps
body:
### Purpose

This issue records the package set and install order used for our Atlas A3 MegaMoe validation on CANN 9.2.0. It is an environment-reproduction note, not a bug report. The related ABI investigation is in #17030.

### Artifact availability

The CANN 9.2.0 and MegaMoe custom artifacts used in this validation are not distributed through this public issue. For reproducibility, request the exact artifacts from Huawei/Ascend and compare their SHA256 values with the table below.

### Validated baseline

- Platform: Atlas A3 / Ascend910_93
- OS/architecture: Linux aarch64
- Python: 3.12.13
- PyTorch: 2.10.0+cpu
- torch_npu: 2.10.0.post4
- vLLM: `v0.27.1`, commit `6e448d0ea9bf3d88d898b65449ca6dc2aec170ac`
- vLLM-Ascend: 0.27.1, commit `5a9de65760563f7d17c19627b647a5106235e057`
- CANN version directory: `/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.2.0`

### Package set

Use these exact artifacts and verify the SHA256 values before installation.

| Package | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---:|---|
| `Ascend-cann-toolkit_9.2.0_linux-aarch64.run` | 1.3 GiB | `2e77883d75c52ae8cdd3ab156ec70a85e94836c625f1654b8227083a7b011998` |
| `Ascend-cann-nnal_9.2.0_linux-aarch64.run` | 423 MiB | `a52f38f8108f8f11234c19a470cc5f5fc40482e1ca886b3a35981927e329ab9c` |
| `Ascend-cann-A3-ops_9.2.0_linux-aarch64.run` | 2.4 GiB | `c871c1592eeeeafeb724f7484be7de63a65da24d1d3d7473a03307af58c80f72` |
| `cann-ops-transformer-custom_linux-aarch64_1.run` | 11 MiB | `e78daf18abc0349c9cf467fcae8670d7c9888eaadbfcebed6ae374e635d8a3ae` |
| `cann_ops_transformer_custom-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl` | 44 KiB | `014070fedd17dd85cacbd5cd4a928a5129b2f6ae6299505f907e8921cdce5229` |

The original local wheel filename ended in `_1.whl`. If copying the artifact, remove the `_1` suffix before `pip install`; otherwise pip interprets the platform tag as `any_1` and reports that the wheel is unsupported.

### 1. Install CANN 9.2.0

Use the recommended clean order below. If a previous CANN installation exists, clean it first and avoid mixing versions.

```bash
PKG_DIR=${PKG_DIR:-/path/to/cann-9.2.0-packages}

"$PKG_DIR/Ascend-cann-toolkit_9.2.0_linux-aarch64.run" --install
"$PKG_DIR/Ascend-cann-nnal_9.2.0_linux-aarch64.run" --install
"$PKG_DIR/Ascend-cann-A3-ops_9.2.0_linux-aarch64.run" --install

source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh
```

After installation:

```bash
readlink -f /usr/local/Ascend/cann
# expected: /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.2.0

python3 -c "import cann_ops_transformer; print(cann_ops_transformer.__file__)"
# expected under /usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.2.0/python/site-packages
```

### 2. Install the MegaMoe custom vendor package

```bash
PKG_DIR=${PKG_DIR:-/path/to/cann-9.2.0-packages}
source /usr/local/Ascend/cann/set_env.sh

"$PKG_DIR/cann-ops-transformer-custom_linux-aarch64_1.run" --force
```

The validated installation has:

```text
/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.2.0/opp/vendors/custom_transformer
load_priority=custom_transformer
```

The vendor `version.info` in the supplied artifact reports:

```text
custom_opp_compiler_version=9.1.0
```

This is the version string of the supplied custom vendor artifact; the validation was run with CANN 9.2.0 and the matching custom wheel described below.

### 3. Install and repair the custom MegaMoe wheel

Install the wheel:

```bash
python3 -m pip install cann_ops_transformer_custom-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl \
  --force-reinstall --no-deps
```

The wheel is not self-contained. Copy the missing Python common package and C++ source from the CANN-installed `cann_ops_transformer` package:

```bash
CANN_HOME=${CANN_HOME:-/usr/local/Ascend/cann}
SITE=/usr/local/python3.12.13/lib/python3.12/site-packages
CUSTOM="$SITE/cann_ops_transformer_custom"
ORIG="$CANN_HOME/python/site-packages/cann_ops_transformer"

# Missing Python module.
rm -rf "$CUSTOM/ops/mc2/common"
cp -a "$ORIG/ops/mc2/common" "$CUSTOM/ops/mc2/common"

# Re-point the copied common module to the custom namespace.
grep -RIl "from cann_ops_transformer\." "$CUSTOM/ops/mc2/common" \
  | xargs -r sed -i 's/from cann_ops_transformer\./from cann_ops_transformer_custom./g'

# Missing C++ source used by CommContextManager.
mkdir -p "$CUSTOM/csrc/mc2"
cp -an "$ORIG/csrc/mc2/comm_context.cpp" "$CUSTOM/csrc/mc2/comm_context.cpp"
cp -an "$ORIG/csrc/mc2/comm_channel_builder_manager.cpp" \
  "$CUSTOM/csrc/mc2/comm_channel_builder_manager.cpp" 2>/dev/null || true

# Prevent common from being treated as an op by auto-discovery.
sed -i 's/_skip = frozenset(("graph_convert",))/_skip = frozenset(("graph_convert", "common"))/' \
  "$CUSTOM/ops/__init__.py"

# Point the custom builder to the custom utils module.
sed -i 's/from cann_ops_transformer.utils.arg_check import wrap_op_module/from cann_ops_transformer_custom.utils.arg_check import wrap_op_module/' \
  "$CUSTOM/op_builder/builder.py"
```

More background on the wheel packaging gap is in #17030.

### 4. vLLM / vLLM-Ascend notes

For the validated setup:

```text
vLLM          = v0.27.1
vLLM-Ascend   = 5a9de65760563f7d17c19627b647a5106235e057
```

No vLLM rebuild is needed. No vLLM-Ascend rebuild is needed for the current validation changes because they are Python-only.

The temporary vLLM-Ascend validation changes are:

1. Prefer the CANN-installed `custom_transformer` vendor over the repo-embedded vendor.
2. Load MegaMoe directly from `cann_ops_transformer_custom.ops.mc2.mega_moe`.

### 5. Minimal smoke result

With this package combination, a 2-NPU MegaMoe loader smoke test passes:

```text
rank=0 sym_buffer created ccl=419430400
rank=1 sym_buffer created ccl=419430400
rank=0 S5_LOADER_SUCCESS out=(8, 1024)
rank=1 S5_LOADER_SUCCESS out=(8, 1024)
```

```text
arch=aarch64
os=linux
path=/usr/local/Ascend/cann-9.1.0
```

</details>

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`MultiConnector` can crash `EngineCore` while reconstructing KV transfer stats, whenever a child connector is registered under a `kv_connector` config name that differs from its Python class name.

The two vllm-ascend connectors that trigger this are:

- `AscendOffloadingConnector` — registered as config name `OffloadingConnector`
- `UCMConnectorV1` — registered as config name `UCMConnector`

#### Why this is a real code path (not a synthetic mismatch)

The worker and logger sides disagree on the key space of the transfer-stats dict:

1. **Worker emits stats keyed by class name.** `multi_connector.py::get_kv_connector_stats()` builds the dict with `connector_id = c.__class__.__name__` (e.g. `"AscendOffloadingConnector"`). `AscendOffloadingConnector` inherits `OffloadingConnector.get_kv_connector_stats()`, which returns `self.connector_scheduler.get_stats()`; so as soon as offloading is enabled this key is always produced. `MultiKVConnectorStats.to_dict()` serializes it unchanged.
2. **Logger resolves that key through the factory, which is keyed by config name.** `metrics.py::KVConnectorLogging.observe()` calls `self.connector_cls.build_kv_connector_stats(transfer_stats_data)`, where `connector_cls` is the configured `MultiConnector` (here `AscendMultiConnector`).
3. **`build_kv_connector_stats` assumes the two key spaces are identical.** It does `KVConnectorFactory.get_connector_class_by_name(connector_name)` with **no try/except**. That lookup succeeds only for connectors whose registration name equals their class name — true for upstream connectors (`OffloadingConnector`, `NixlConnector`, …) and for `AscendStoreConnector`, but false for the two connectors above.

So this is not a matter of preference: the invariant "every key the worker emits is a registered connector name" is violated by a plugin that overrides an upstream connector with a differently-named class. The result is an unhandled `ValueError` on the stats interval path, which per the field report propagates out of `AsyncLLM.output_handler` and tears down `EngineCore` (in-flight requests then fail with HTTP 500).

The same applies to `UCMConnectorV1`. Note that `AscendSimpleCPUOffloadConnector` (config name `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`) is **not** affected: it does not override `get_kv_connector_stats`, and the base implementation returns `None`, so no stats key is ever emitted for it.

#### Minimal reproduction (CPU, no NPU required)

The defect is a pure registry-lookup mismatch, so it reproduces on any machine with `vllm==0.28.0` installed. The payload below is exactly what the worker produces in production and what `KVConnectorLogging.observe()` passes on:

```python
from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.multi_connector import MultiConnector

# Keyed by __class__.__name__, as produced by get_kv_connector_stats().
MultiConnector.build_kv_connector_stats({"AscendOffloadingConnector": {"data": {}}})
```

Result:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 4, in <module>
  File ".../vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py", line 608, in build_kv_connector_stats
    connector_cls = KVConnectorFactory.get_connector_class_by_name(
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File ".../vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/factory.py", line 92, in get_connector_class_by_name
    raise ValueError(f"Connector '{connector_name}' is not registered.")
ValueError: Connector 'AscendOffloadingConnector' is not registered.
```

(Line numbers are from the installed `vllm==0.28.0`; on current `main` the failing call is around `multi_connector.py:639`.)

#### End-to-end manifestation

On the reported deployment (1P1D, `MultiConnector(MooncakeConnectorV1 + OffloadingConnector)`, host-DRAM offload enabled), the first stats interval after a request produces this `ValueError`, the engine exits, and the request returns 500. Patching the registry lookup to resolve the class name yields zero such errors over a full benchmark run.

#### Fix direction

Two complementary changes:

- **vllm-ascend**: register the class names as aliases (`AscendOffloadingConnector`, `UCMConnectorV1`) so the existing lookup resolves — proposed in #16930.
- **vLLM (upstream)**: `MultiConnector.build_kv_connector_stats()` should not hard-fail on a key it cannot resolve; it should skip unknown connectors with a warning and keep the remaining stats. The introducing PR vllm-project/vllm#27366 described exactly this "skip with warning" behavior, but the merged code has no such guard.

#### Workaround

For deployments that cannot wait for the fix, re-register the alias in `vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/__init__.py::register_connector()` or re-apply the container-level patch described in the internal ops note for this deployment.

title: [Doc]: Incorrect Description of Usage Scenario for AscendStoreConnector load_async
body:
### 📚 The doc issue

 Environment： vllm-ascend 0.23.0 ~ latest

## Describe problem
In `docs/source/tutorials/models/GLM5.2.md`, the description of `load_async` is inconsistent with the actual code logic.

- Line 1159: the `AscendStoreConnector` has `kv_role` set to `kv_consumer` (Decode node) and configures `"load_async": true`;
- Line 1246: `"load_async": true` (decode side): Asynchronously loads KV cache from the pool on decode nodes.

Both places describe `load_async` as a feature of the **Decode (kv_consumer) node**, but in reality, asynchronously loading KV cache from the KV Pool happens on the **Prefill (kv_producer) node** — when the prefix cache hits the external cache, the Prefill node uses `load_async` to asynchronously load the external KV cache, avoiding redundant prefill computation.

## Code evidence

`vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_pool/ascend_store/pool_scheduler.py`:

```python
def get_num_new_matched_tokens(...) -> tuple[int, bool]:
    ...
    if self.kv_role == "kv_consumer" and not self.consumer_is_to_load:
        return 0, False   # Decode node defaults to consumer_is_to_load=False, so it does not load
```

As shown:

- `kv_producer` (Prefill) does not satisfy this condition, so it normally performs the load logic (loading from the KV Pool on a prefix-cache hit);
- `kv_consumer` (Decode) defaults to `consumer_is_to_load=False`, so it does **not** load from the KV Pool (Decode mainly gets KV via Mooncake P2P transfer).

Therefore, the "asynchronously load external cache" capability of `load_async` actually serves the **Prefill node**, not the Decode node.

### Suggest a potential alternative/fix


1. Change line 1246 to:

   > `"load_async": true` (prefill side): Asynchronously loads KV cache from the pool on prefill nodes when the prefix cache hits the external KV Pool.

2. For the Decode-node configuration around line 1159, please confirm whether `load_async` should be kept there or moved to the Prefill-node configuration (if the Decode node really needs to load from the KV Pool, it should explicitly set `consumer_is_to_load: true`).

title: [Bug]: DeepSeek V4 Preview checkpoints receive post-Preview reasoning-effort prompts
body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM Ascend branch: `releases/v0.26.0rc` at `820a21d6593b74211863c7787e1ba9b4deaf9126`
- vLLM version: `v0.26.0`
- Regression introduced by #13993 and still present after #14624
- Reproduction is tokenizer-only; the user-visible impact was found by the DeepSeek V4 Flash GPQA smoke test

### Describe the bug

The DeepSeek V4 thinking patch added by #13993 unconditionally applies the post-Preview reasoning-effort mapping to every DeepSeek V4 checkpoint.

The official DeepSeek V4 Preview encoders and the encoders shipped with later checkpoints such as DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 use different meanings for the same effort names:

| Requested effort | V4 Preview prompt | Post-Preview prompt |
|---|---|---|
| `high` (also the API default) | no effort prefix | `Reasoning Effort: Absolute maximum...` |
| `max` / `xhigh` | `Reasoning Effort: Absolute maximum...` | `max` uses `Reasoning Effort: Beyond maximum...`; `xhigh` maps to post-Preview high |

After #13993, a V4 Preview request with omitted effort or explicit `high` therefore receives the prompt that its own encoder associates with maximum effort. In the GPQA smoke test with thinking enabled and `max_tokens=131072`, this produces many truncated answers and lowers accuracy.

This is a checkpoint compatibility regression in the reasoning-effort patch. It is separate from the system/tools placement bug reported in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51829.

A tokenizer-only probe on the current release branch shows the incorrect behavior before the fix:

```text
DeepSeek-V4-Flash (Preview):
  default: absolute-maximum
  high: absolute-maximum
  max: beyond-maximum
```

The checkpoint generations can be distinguished from `config.json` without relying on model path names:

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Pro Preview have no `dspark_*` fields.
- DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 contain `dspark_block_size`, `dspark_markov_rank`, `dspark_noise_token_id`, and `dspark_target_layer_ids`.

Expected behavior:

1. If `config.json` contains any `dspark_*` field, use the post-Preview mapping added by #13993.
2. Otherwise, preserve the V4 Preview mapping: default/high has no effort prefix, while max/xhigh uses the original `Absolute maximum` prefix.
3. Explicit thinking disablement must continue to override the requested effort.

Regression coverage should verify both mapping tables and the exact prompt prefix for Preview default/high/max and post-Preview high/max.

title: [Bug]: vllm serve hangs with vector core timeout (507034) on DP>1 when FlashComm1 (SP) and multistream_overlap_shared_expert are both enabled
body:
### Your current environment

<details>
<summary>Environment</summary>

```text
- vLLM: 0.28.0 (built into image vllm-ascend:v0.28.0-a3-openeuler)
- vLLM-Ascend: main @ d4d2957e5 (editable install; also reproduced on f640d1348 and on the image built-in version)
- CANN: cann-9.1.0
- torch: 2.10.0+cpu / torch_npu: 2.10.0.post4
- Hardware: Atlas 800 A3 (Ascend 910B x 16), single node
- OS: openEuler (docker)
- Model: GLM-5.2-w4a8c8 (W4A8, --quantization ascend)
```

</details>

### Describe the bug

`vllm serve` with `--data-parallel-size 2 --tensor-parallel-size 8` hangs during engine initialization (memory profiling / dummy run) and dies with:

```text
RuntimeError: synchronize:../torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/NPUEvent.cpp:215 NPU function error: aclrtSynchronizeEvent(event_), error code is 507034
[Error]: Vector core execution timed out.
```

This happens **only when all three factors are present simultaneously**:

1. `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1=1` (env var, i.e. SP enabled)
2. `multistream_overlap_shared_expert: true` (in `--additional-config`)
3. `--data-parallel-size > 1`

Removing **any one** of the three makes the service start normally. Verified with a 12-experiment matrix (below), each run on a clean 16-card machine (HBM baseline confirmed before each run).

Independently excluded (failure persists with each of these removed/changed):
- `enable_sfa_prolog_v3`, `enable_dsa_cp`, `enable_sparse_li_c8` / `enable_sparse_sfa_c8` (none present in the minimal repro)
- MTP speculative decoding (present in the passing minimal repro; disabling it does not rescue the failing combo)
- cudagraph `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` (failing combo still dies with `--enforce-eager`)
- vLLM-Ascend version (main @ d4d2957e5, main @ f640d1348, and image built-in all fail; same code passes with DP=1)
- `LD_PRELOAD` jemalloc

### Verification matrix

| # | FLASHCOMM1 (SP) | multistream_overlap_shared_expert | extra additional-config | DP | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | - | - | (empty) | 2 | PASS (starts in ~4 min) |
| 2 | - | - | balance_scheduling | 2 | PASS |
| 3 | - | - | fused_mc2:0 | 2 | PASS |
| 4 | yes | - | (empty) | 2 | PASS |
| 5 | - | yes | (empty) | 2 | PASS |
| 9 | yes | - | balance_scheduling | 2 | PASS |
| 12 | yes | - | fused_mc2:0 | 2 | PASS |
| **11** | **yes** | **yes** | **(empty)** | **2** | **FAIL - 507034 vector core timeout, ~13 min into init** |
| 10 | yes | yes | + fused_mc2:0 | 2 | FAIL |
| 8 | yes | yes | + balance + fused_mc2 | 2 | FAIL |
| ctrl-A | yes | yes | full prod config (c8 etc.) | 1 (TP16) | PASS |
| ctrl-B | - | yes | DSv4-Flash tutorial A3 config | 2 (TP8) | PASS (different model, no FlashComm1) |

### To Reproduce

Failing command (GLM-5.2-w4a8c8, single node 16x 910B):

```bash
export VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1=1
vllm serve /path/to/GLM-5.2-w4a8c8 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8177 \
  --safetensors-load-strategy prefetch --api-server-count 1 \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --seed 1024 --served-model-name glm-5 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --max-num-seqs 12 --max-model-len 135000 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --quantization ascend \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}' \
  --additional-config '{"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true}' \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":3,"method":"deepseek_mtp","enforce_eager":true}'
```

The exact same command starts normally if either `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1` is unset, or `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` is removed from `--additional-config`, or `--data-parallel-size 1` (TP16) is used.

### Error log

```text
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR [multiproc_executor.py:1047] Traceback (most recent call last):
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py", line 1039, in worker_busy_loop
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR   File ".../vllm_ascend/worker/worker.py", line 600, in determine_available_memory
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR     self.model_runner.profile_run()
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR   File ".../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 4041, in profile_run
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR     super().profile_run()
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR   File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 6618, in profile_run
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR     hidden_states, last_hidden_states = self._dummy_run(...)
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR   File ".../vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py", line 3771, in _dummy_run
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR     with self.synchronize_input_prep():
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR   File ".../torch_npu/npu/streams.py", line 192, in synchronize
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR RuntimeError: synchronize:../torch_npu/csrc/core/npu/NPUEvent.cpp:215 NPU function error: aclrtSynchronizeEvent(event_), error code is 507034
(Worker_DP1_TP1_EP9 pid=xxxxx) ERROR [Error]: Vector core execution timed out.
```

Workers across **both DP ranks** fail at the same second (~13 min after launch, during `determine_available_memory -> profile_run -> _dummy_run`). Sometimes also accompanied by `HCCL watchdog thread terminated with exception`.

### Expected behavior

The service should start normally with FlashComm1 (SP) + `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` on DP>1, as it does with DP=1 (TP16) under the identical configuration.

### Additional context

- Hypothesis: an interaction between the FlashComm1 (SP) communication path and the shared-expert side stream (`npu_stream_switch(shared_experts_calculation_stream())` in `vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/fused_moe.py`) deadlocks during the DP dummy run and surfaces as a vector core timeout.
- Impact note for users: `enable_dsa_cp` **requires** SP (`vllm_ascend/utils.py:1558` raises `ValueError` if FlashComm1 is off), so users who need DSA CP cannot drop FlashComm1 - their only workaround on DP>1 today is to disable `multistream_overlap_shared_expert`.
- Related interplay: `enable_fused_mc2=1` force-disables `multistream_overlap_shared_expert` (with a warning) in `ascend_config.py`, so the fused_mc2 path is presumably unaffected.
- Environment detail: reproduced consistently across two days (2026-09-12 / 09-13), >6 failing runs, all on a freshly verified idle machine; the passing runs prove the stack itself is healthy.

# [Bug] MegaMoe on Kimi K3 (A3, PD-disaggregated 4P4D) produces garbled output and vector-core crash (acl error 507035) ## Summary When enabling MegaMoe (`enable_fused_mc2: 2` + `enable_prefill_mc2: true`) for Kimi K3 W4A8 on Atlas 800I A3, **every request returns garbled tokens**, and the prefill nodes eventually **crash with an AI-vector-core exception (`aclrtSynchronizeEvent` error 507035)** followed by glibc heap corruption (`corrupted size vs. prev_size`) on shutdown. Disabling MegaMoe on the exact same build/environment produces correct output — so the problem is isolated to the MegaMoe path. **Important note**: MegaMoe enablement for Kimi K3 was **cherry-picked** as commit `5a9de6576` ("feat(moe): enable MegaMoe for Kimi K3") on top of the v0.27.1rc nightly (`67dd25526`). We are not sure whether the issue is introduced by the picked changes or by the interaction between the picked code and the CANN weekly ops package — the full diff of the pick is attached below. ## Environment - Hardware: Atlas 800I A3 (910_93), 8 nodes x 16 NPU - Deployment: **PD-disaggregated 4P4D**, both sides DP4/TP16 + DCP16, MooncakeConnectorV1 KV transfer, dspark speculative decoding (draft=7) - vLLM: 0.27.1 (editable install) - vllm-ascend: 0.27.1 (editable install, nightly `67dd25526` = `0.19.1rc2.dev1908` + cherry-pick `5a9de6576`) - CANN: 9.3.0 weekly `20260916.01` (the A3-ops package bundles `cann-A3-ops-transformer_9.2.0`) - torch_npu / torch: image-bundled (torch_npu 2.10.0) ## Complete configuration ### Deployment topology & startup order - 8 nodes, all in the same supernode (43117103): 4 Prefill (P0-P3) + 4 Decode (D0-D3) - Startup order: `mooncake_master` (P0, port 50088) -> 4x prefill `vllm serve` (DP rendezvous, RANK=0..3) -> 4x decode `vllm serve` -> load-balance proxy (P0, port 1999) - Per node: exactly 1 `vllm serve` process, TP16 occupies the node's 16 NPUs - Benchmark requests enter through the proxy on P0:1999 ### Full vllm serve command (prefill node, RANK=0) ```bash vllm serve /home/admin/model-csi/model \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \ --tokenizer-mode kimi_k3 \ --data-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-rank 0 \ --nnodes 4 --node-rank 0 \ --data-parallel-rpc-port 29500 --master-addr 172.16.136.213 \ --tensor-parallel-size 16 \ --decode-context-parallel-size 16 \ --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 384 --block-size 384 \ --enable-expert-parallel --seed 1024 \ --served-model-name kimi-k3 \ --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 16 \ --trust-remote-code --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1":true,"enable_shared_expert_dp":false,"multistream_overlap_shared_expert":true,"enable_fused_mc2":2,"enable_prefill_mc2":true,"mega_moe_max_tokens":8192}' \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 1 --quantization ascend --mm-encoder-tp-mode data \ --skip-mm-profiling --enforce-eager \ --safetensors_load_strategy prefetch \ --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"vision_chunk":40}' \ --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"...","torch_profiler_with_stack":false}' \ --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"MultiConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_connector_extra_config":{"connectors":[{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnectorV1","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_buffer_device":"npu","kv_port":"50012","kv_connector_extra_config":{"prefill":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":16},"decode":{"dp_size":4,"tp_size":16}}}]}}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/home/admin/draft-model","num_speculative_tokens":7,"draft_tensor_parallel_size":16,"max_model_len":4096,"draft_sample_method":"greedy","enforce_eager":true}' ``` Decode nodes use the same parallel settings with `--all2all-backend allgather_reducescatter --dtype bfloat16 --async-scheduling --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[16,32,48,64,80,96,112,128],"cudagraph_num_of_warmups":1}'` and `kv_role: kv_consumer`; **decode additional_config has `enable_fused_mc2: false`** (MegaMoe off on D side for this test). ### additional_config (as passed on the command line) - Prefill: `{"enable_flashcomm1": true, "enable_shared_expert_dp": false, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "enable_fused_mc2": 2, "enable_prefill_mc2": true, "mega_moe_max_tokens": 8192}` - Decode: `{"enable_cpu_binding": false, "enable_shared_expert_dp": false, "multistream_overlap_shared_expert": true, "enable_fused_mc2": false, "enable_prefill_mc2": false, "enable_reduce_sample": false, "finegrained_tp_config": {"lmhead_tensor_parallel_size": 0}, Launch the PD service with the config above (prefill side MegaMoe enabled). 2. Startup completes normally. Symm-buffer allocation log shows the MC2 group spans **64 EP ranks across the 4 prefill nodes**: ``` CANN MegaMoe sym-buffer alloc (must match across all EP ranks): ep_rank=0 ep_world=64 global_bs=0 ``` 3. Send any request (even `1+1=?`, max_tokens=24, greedy) through the API. 4. **Actual**: response is garbled tokens. Repeated requests garble every time. On the first run (right after a fresh JIT build of the custom ops), all 4 prefill API servers aborted ~1 min after the first request. 5. **Expected**: coherent output (the identical request returns a correct answer when MegaMoe is disabled). ## Evidence ### Garbled output (greedy, `1+1=?`) ``` 有损gt迫不及待=""; |string \(alist : Cler宇航пер自行车数十万帮我们田里也不算龙王α... ``` Second request (`What is 2+3?`): ``` .mmNa很高兴吸音 ngx별yla_TFequal函》。 ****** █iers或其它 ``` ### Vector-core crash dump (error 507035) ``` EE9999: rtStreamSynchronize execution failed, reason=vector core exception RuntimeError: aclrtSynchronizeEvent(event_), error code is 507035 [Error]: The vector core execution is abnormal. EZ9999: An error occurs on the device(chipId:2, dieId:0), the serial number is 9, the error is aivec error, core id is 35, error code = 0, dump info: pc start: 0x12c0c1600000, current: 0x12c0c1600478, vec error info: 0x731e7c8f24, mte error info: 0x9034aa2022, ifu error info: 0x3ec68ff329180, ccu error info: 0xc1a9c65972d38f45, cube error info: 0, biu error info: 0, ... ``` Multiple vector cores (34-40) faulted with the same `pc start` (same kernel). `cube error info: 0` — the cube cores are clean, so the faulting task is a **vector kernel** inside the MegaMoe chain. plog confirms the failing task is **not** an HCCL task: ``` [TaskExceptionHandler][Callback] begin to execute hccl task exception callback function. stream not found. the fail task is not from HCCL. streamid[47] ``` ### Suspicious runtime warning: symm buffer far below the documented safe bound ``` WARNING [moe_comm_method.py:330] MegaMoe symm buffer: max_recv_token_num is set from mega_moe_max_tokens=8192 (reference value) on a P or PD-mixed node. If the actual per-rank received token count after dispatch exceeds this value, precision degradation will occur. The absolute safe upper bound is 458752 (num_max_tokens_per_rank=512, ep_world_size=64, num_topk=16, expert_per_rank=14). ``` `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` was set ~56x below the safe upper bound (458752). We suspect this contributes to the garbled output (the code comment explicitly says "precision degradation will occur" on overflow), though even a tiny `1+1=?` request garbles, which suggests the problem may be deeper than a plain buffer overflow. ### Shutdown heap corruption After the vector-core fault, the API servers die with: ``` [shutdown] MPClient: complete corrupted size vs. prev_size (glibc abort, "Aborted (core dumped)") ``` ## Isolation test Same code build + same CANN 9.3.0 weekly, only difference = MegaMoe flags: | Config | Result | |---|---| | `enable_fused_mc2: 2` + `enable_prefill_mc2: true` | garbled output on every request; vector-core crash (507035) on first run | | `enable_fused_mc2: false` | correct output (both direct prefill-node request and full P→D path through the load-balance proxy) | Decode-only nodes with the same build but MegaMoe disabled run stable throughout. ## What we ruled out - Attention path change: DSA-CP disabled in both runs, attention identical - KV transfer / decode side: garbled output occurs on a direct prefill-node request that never touches the decode cluster - HCCL comm kernel: plog says the failing task is not from HCCL - SiTUGLU support: the weekly `cann_ops_transformer` `mega_moe` signature exposes `activation`/`activation_params`, so the capability check passes - W4A8 weight packing: `w4a8.py` applies `maybe_trans_nz()` before building `cann_mega_moe_*_weight_list` ## Suspicions 1. `mega_moe_max_tokens=8192` far below the safe upper bound (458752) — but the tiny-request garble suggests something more 2. Version mismatch between the picked code and the weekly CANN package (`cann-A3-ops-transformer_9.2.0` bundled inside 9.3.0 weekly) — the picked code mentions SiTUGLU requires "ops-transformer commit 0a5860c or newer" 3. title: [Bug][v0.26.0rc1] DeepSeek-V4 prefix caching 0% hit rate for prompts shorter than 4096 tokens due to C4 compressor state cache block_size=2
body:
### Your current environment

```text
vLLM-Ascend: v0.26.0rc1
vLLM: v0.26.0
Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8
Hardware: Atlas 800 A3 (TP=8)
CANN: 9.1.0
PyTorch / torch_npu: 2.10.0 / 2.10.0.post4
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

DeepSeek-V4 prefix caching produces **0% cache hit rate** for prompts shorter than 4096 tokens, despite `enable_prefix_caching=True` being set. The root cause is that the C4 compressor state cache (`block_size=2`, `prefix_cacheable=True`) drags down the global `cache_config.block_size` to 2 via `min(participating)`, and the C128 main cache group's `block_size=4096` causes `scheduler_block_size = LCM(128, 4096, 32, 2, 8) = 4096`. Cache writes and hits are aligned to `scheduler_block_size`, so `round_down(2048, 4096) = 0` — no tokens are ever registered in the prefix cache hash map for small prompts.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start vLLM with the following command (without `--kv-transfer-config`):

```bash
vllm serve /home/weight/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-w8a8 \
  --max_model_len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --served-model-name dsv4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --enable-expert-parallel \
  --enable-prefix-caching \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \
  --quantization ascend \
  --port 8900 \
  --block-size 32 \
  --speculative-config '{"num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"dspark","enforce_eager":true}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

2. Send two identical requests with a 2048-token prompt:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8900/v1/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"dsv4","prompt":"<2048-token text>","max_tokens":5,"temperature":0}' | python3 -m json.tool
```

3. Check metrics:

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8900/metrics | grep -E 'prefix_cache_hits|cache_config_info'
```

### Observed behavior

**Metrics show `block_size` is overridden from 32 to 2:**

```
vllm:cache_config_info{block_size="2",user_specified_block_size="True",_block_size_resolved="True",enable_prefix_caching="True",prefix_match_unit="None",sliding_window="128",...}
```

**Prefix cache hit rate is 0% for 2K inputs, 49.5% for 8K inputs:**

| Input length | prefix_cache_queries | prefix_cache_hits | Hit rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2K (2048 tokens) | 136,387 | 0 | **0.00%** |
| 8K (8192 tokens) | 537,878 | 266,240 | **49.50%** |

**API response `cached_tokens` is always 0 for small prompts, even on repeated identical requests:**

```json
// Request 1 (cold cache)
{"usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1843, "completion_tokens": 5, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}}}

// Request 2 (same prompt, should hit cache)
{"usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1843, "completion_tokens": 5, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}}}

// Request 3 (same prompt again)
{"usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1843, "completion_tokens": 5, "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 0}}}
```

**KV cache blocks are allocated during the request but released immediately after the request completes:**

```
During request:  kv_cache_usage_perc = 0.086314
0.6s after end:   kv_cache_usage_perc = 0.000000  (blocks released, hash lost)
```

### Expected behavior

- `cache_config.block_size` should not be dragged down to 2 by the C4 compressor state cache
- Prefix cache should produce non-zero hit rates for prompts shorter than 4096 tokens
- `cached_tokens` in API response should reflect actual cache hits

### Root cause analysis

DeepSeek-V4 has 5 KV cache groups with different block sizes:

| Group | block_size | prefix_cacheable | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| MLA C4 main cache | 128 | True | `storage_block_size(32) × compress_ratio(4)` |
| MLA C128 main cache | 4096 | True | `storage_block_size(32) × compress_ratio(128)` |
| SWA cache | 32 | True | `DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES[32][0][1]` |
| **C4 compressor state cache** | **2** | **True (inherited)** | `DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES[32][0][2]` |
| C128 compressor state cache | 8 | True | `DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES[32][0][3]` |

**Problem 1: `cache_config.block_size = 2`**

In `vllm/v1/engine/core.py:340-349`, vLLM core computes:
```python
participating = [
    g.kv_cache_spec.block_size
    for g in kv_cache_groups
    if g.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable
]
cache_config.block_size = min(participating)  # min(128, 4096, 32, 2, 8) = 2
```

The C4 compressor state cache has `block_size=2` and inherits `prefix_cacheable=True` from `AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec → SlidingWindowMLASpec → SlidingWindowSpec → KVCacheSpec` (no override). This drags the global `block_size` down to 2.

Note: vLLM upstream already has precedent for excluding scratch buffers — `KpoolTailSpec` and `CircularBufferSpec` both override `prefix_cacheable = False` for exactly this reason. The engine core comment (lines 336-339) explicitly warns about this pattern but the C4 state cache is not excluded.

**Problem 2: `scheduler_block_size = 4096`**

In `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`, vLLM computes:
```python
scheduler_block_size = math.lcm(*group_block_sizes)  # LCM(128, 4096, 32, 2, 8) = 4096
```

This is computed over ALL groups (including non-cacheable ones), which is correct by design. However, it means cache writes and hits are aligned to 4096 tokens:

```python
# vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py:764
def _align_cacheable(self, num_tokens: int) -> int:
    return round_down(num_tokens, self.scheduler_block_size)
```

| Prompt length | `round_down(_, 4096)` | Tokens cached | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2K (2048) | **0** | 0 | 0% hit |
| 8K (8192) | **8192** | 8192 | ~50% hit |

The 4096 comes from the C128 main cache group (`block_size = 32 × 128 = 4096`), which is inherent to DeepSeek-V4's `compress_ratio=128`.

### Impact

- Prefix caching is completely non-functional for workloads with prompt length < 4096 tokens
- `cached_tokens` in API responses is always 0 for small prompts, making per-request cache-based billing impossible
- No TTFT improvement from prefix caching for short-prompt workloads
- The `block_size=2` metric is misleading and may affect other subsystems

### Workaround

Use input prompts with ≥ 4096 tokens. In our testing, 8K input with 90% prefix overlap achieves 49.5% cache hit rate.

### Additional context

- vLLM version: v0.26.0
- vLLM-Ascend version: v0.26.0rc1
- Related upstream code: `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` (block_size resolution), `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` (LCM/GCD), `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py` (_align_cacheable)
- Related vllm-ascend code: `vllm_ascend/core/kv_cache_interface.py` (AscendSlidingWindowMLASpec), `vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v4/compressor.py` (AscendCompressorStateCache.get_kv_cache_spec), `vllm_ascend/models/layer/attention/layer.py` (_DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES)

title: [Bug]: Qwen3.8-27B在910B2部署fc任务工具参数结果中出现错误json格式
[Bug]: [v0.23.0]: bundled legacy qwen3_xml parser emits whitespace-only content before first tool call
body:
### Your current environment

### Environment

- Image: quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:v0.23.0
- vLLM: upstream v0.23.0
- Base image from the release Dockerfile: quay.io/ascend/cann:9.1.0-910b-ubuntu22.04-py3.12
- Hardware: Ascend NPU (the image is the 910B Ubuntu variant)
- Mode: streaming chat completion with Qwen3 XML tool calling
- Affected file inside the image: /vllm-workspace/vllm/vllm/tool_parsers/qwen3xml_tool_parser.py
- The model and cache directories are mounted; the affected vLLM source file is part of the image filesystem.

The host and container names are omitted because they are internal deployment details.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

### Summary

The official v0.23.0 Ascend image bundles the legacy Qwen3XMLToolParser from upstream vLLM v0.23.0. When the model finishes thinking and starts a tool call with a whitespace separator, the streaming parser emits a whitespace-only buffer as normal assistant content.

This causes the frontend to receive an extra Markdown/content delta containing "\\n\\n" before the tool call.

### Minimal reproduction

Model output:

~~~xml
<think>
...
</think>

<tool_call>
<function=get_weather>
<parameter=city>Tokyo</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
~~~

The relevant stream boundary is:

~~~text
1. "\\n\\n"
2. "<tool_call>"
3. "<function=get_weather>..."
~~~

Actual streaming result:

~~~text
reasoning_content: "..."
content: "\\n\\n"
tool_calls: [...]
~~~

Expected result:

~~~text
reasoning_content: "..."
content: null / no content delta for the separator
tool_calls: [...]
~~~

### Affected logic

There are two flush paths in qwen3xml_tool_parser.py:

1. In parse_single_streaming_chunks(), a non-empty text_content_buffer is emitted as content whenever tool_call_index == 0. A whitespace-only buffer is therefore emitted before the first tool call.
2. In _process_complete_xml_elements(), the first <tool_call> unconditionally flushes a non-empty text_content_buffer, including when it contains only whitespace.

### Proposed minimal fix

Only suppress the buffer when the complete buffered value is whitespace. Preserve real text before a tool call, for example "I will query this first:\\n\\n".

~~~diff
- if self.text_content_buffer and self.tool_call_index == 0:
+ if (
+     self.text_content_buffer
+     and self.text_content_buffer.strip()
+     and self.tool_call_index == 0
+ ):
      text_delta = DeltaMessage(content=self.text_content_buffer)
      self._emit_delta(text_delta)
      self.text_content_buffer = ""
      return text_delta
~~~

At the first-tool-call flush path, apply the same check before emitting and always clear the buffer afterward:

~~~python
if (...) and self.text_content_buffer:
    if self.text_content_buffer.strip():
        text_delta = DeltaMessage(content=self.text_content_buffer)
        self._emit_delta(text_delta)
    self.text_content_buffer = ""
~~~

The intended behavior is not to discard whitespace globally: non-whitespace content before a tool call must remain content, while a whitespace-only separator should not create a content delta.

### Source/provenance

The vllm-ascend v0.23.0 release Dockerfile clones upstream vLLM with VLLM_TAG=v0.23.0 and then copies the vLLM Ascend plugin into the image:

- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/blob/v0.23.0/Dockerfile
- The affected file in upstream vLLM v0.23.0: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/vllm/tool_parsers/qwen3xml_tool_parser.py
- The upstream Qwen3 XML tests mark multiple streaming cases as having systematic/known streaming issues: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.23.0/tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3xml_tool_parser.py

I first reported this to upstream vLLM in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55633. The upstream maintainer confirmed that this legacy parser is no longer present on current main and suggested reporting the issue against the release/downstream artifact carrying it.

Could you please confirm whether this should be fixed/backported for the v0.23.0 release image, or documented as a known limitation?

title: [Bug]: Hybrid GDN models (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B): long prefills serialize with default max_num_batched_tokens=2048 (<70GB branch) + mamba align mode
body:
### What happened?

Serving a hybrid GDN model (**Qwen3.6-35B-A3B**, INT4 W4A16, 40 layers: linear-attention/GDN + full attention) on Atlas 800 A3 with `--enable-prefix-caching` (mamba cache mode resolves to `align`): **concurrent long prefills are scheduled strictly one at a time.**

During a burst of 4 concurrent ~7.5k-token prefills (unique prompts, `max_tokens=2`), `vllm:num_requests_running` **peaks at 1** while the other 3 sit in `waiting` (sampled every 0.5 s from `/metrics`), and wall time equals the sum of individual latencies. Decode-only concurrency is unaffected (6 concurrent short requests → `running=6`).

**Counter-evidence on CUDA:** the same checkpoint with the same flags on the same upstream vLLM version (official `vllm-openai` **v0.28.0**, 2× RTX 3090 TP=2, FP8 weights, `--enable-prefix-caching`) does **not** show this cap — during an identical burst the running gauge climbs well above 1 (the instance also serves unrelated background traffic) and long prefills overlap with other requests.

Disabling prefix caching (no mamba `align` path) raises the long-prefill concurrency cap from 1 to only 2 on Ascend (measured on the v0.27.1-based nightly), so the hard serialization is tied to the align-mode prefill path.

This was verified on **both** the v0.27.1-based nightly (image from ~2026-09-16) and the current nightly with the **vLLM v0.28.0** base — the serialization persists across both, while CUDA v0.28.0 batches prefills. So this looks Ascend-plugin-specific rather than an upstream scheduler limitation.

### Reproduce

```bash
docker run -d --name qwen36-35b-test --shm-size 32g \
  -e ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 -p 8015:8000 \
  -v /usr/local/dcmi:/usr/local/dcmi \
  -v /usr/local/bin/npu-smi:/usr/local/bin/npu-smi \
  -v /etc/ascend_install.info:/etc/ascend_install.info \
  -v /data2/models:/data2/models \
  -v /usr/local/Ascend/driver:/usr/local/Ascend/driver \
  --device /dev/davinci3 --device /dev/davinci_manager \
  --device /dev/devmm_svm --device /dev/hisi_hdc \
  quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main-a3 \
  vllm serve /data2/models/Avesed/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-INT4-W4A16 \
    --served-model-name Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
    --tensor-parallel-size 1 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml --enable-auto-tool-choice \
    --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":0,"video":0}' \
    --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 131072 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

Then fire 4 concurrent requests (~7.5k-token prompts, e.g. a system prompt of `"文档{i}：" + "接口定义与数据流程说明。" * 1500`, `max_tokens=2`, `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}`) and poll `/metrics` at 0.5 s:

```
vllm:num_requests_running  → peaks at 1
vllm:num_requests_waiting  → peaks at 3
```

Control on CUDA (same model family, FP8, same flags): `running` exceeds 1 during the same burst.

### Observed vs expected

| setup | long-prefill burst (4 concurrent ~7.5k tok) |
| --- | --- |
| A3 nightly, vLLM 0.27.1 base, APC on | `running=1`, serialized |
| A3 nightly, **vLLM 0.28.0** base, APC on | `running=1`, serialized |
| CUDA v0.28.0 (official image), APC on | `running` > 1, prefills batched |
| A3 nightly, vLLM 0.27.1 base, **APC off** | `running=2` (better, still not full) |

Expected: align-mode prefill chunks from different requests should be schedulable into the same step (upstream shares the token budget across concurrent prefills on CUDA; cf. the block-aligned chunk splitting and its concurrency fix in vLLM #51113).

### Environment

- Atlas 800 A3 node (`SOC_VERSION=ascend910_9391`, 64 GB × 16 chips), driver/npu-smi 26.1.0, CANN 9.1.0
- Image: `quay.io/ascend/vllm-ascend:nightly-main-a3`, digest `sha256:50451593c500f8b130660bb65028271e03bca1a03aae21508ed8d568b8e99689` (built 2026-09-18)
- `vllm==0.28.0+empty`, `vllm_ascend==0.19.1rc2.dev2256+gc8addbb24`, `torch_npu==2.10.0.post4`, triton-ascend 3.2.2
- One replica per chip (TP=1); also reproduced with the v0.27.1-based nightly from the same tag

### Additional context

- No accuracy problems observed; outputs are correct on both stacks. The issue is purely scheduling throughput for long prefills.
- We see this in production behind multi-turn/agent traffic where several long prompts arrive together; TTFT of requests 2..N is effectively the sum of all prefills.
- Happy to run candidate patches, capture ascend profiler traces, or test specific branches on A3.
